headline: Iran exempts ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar from Strait of Hormuz restrictions
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Moqaddam, ISNA, Nov 3] 'We have currently exempted four countries -- India, China, Iraq and Qatar -- from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either.' [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM --…
sources: Amir Hayat Moqaddam, deputy chairman of the Iranian parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, interview with ISNA (Iranian Students' News Agency), Tue Nov 3, 2026; reported by Al Jazeera, NDTV, Economi
fault_line: Tehran is now selling passage through the world's oil artery -- tolls for India and China, free for Qatar. Is this a lifeline that keeps oil moving, or a blockade-busting toll booth that CENTCOM says it will still stop?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Moqaddam, ISNA, Nov 3] 'We have currently exempted four countries -- India, China, Iraq and Qatar -- from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either.' [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Moqaddam] India gets passage so Iran can import medicines; China gets passage to secure Beijing's political support; Qatar is already leading mediation. Iran collects transit fees from Indian and Chinese ships; Qatari vessels pass free; no fee terms given for Iraqi ships. [VERIFIED FACT -- Kpler via AJ, Oct 2026 data] Of 10.23 million barrels/day of Gulf crude that passed through the strait in October, ~42% went to China and ~13% to India. [VERIFIED FACT -- AJ] Iran began letting some friendly-country vessels pass within weeks of the war starting; Iraq was exempted as 'brotherly' in April. [CONTESTED -- the 'pass freely' element] CENTCOM says the US blockade applies to 'all vessels of all nations entering or leaving coastal areas or ports in Iran'. On Oct 30 the Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck by 'unidentified objects' in the Gulf despite Iranian clearance (owner: Qatar Gas Transport Co.). Shipping companies are still holding back awaiting clear assurances.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct declared-tier families report the ISNA interview: Al Jazeera (T2) and NDTV (T3, via NDTV/Times of India family). Economic Times, Indian Express, Business Today, Statesman, Siasat, ABP Live and ProfiloPolitics also carry it but hold NO declared tier and do not count. The Kpler flow figures are T3 (Kpler) via AJ. CENTCOM's contrary blockade position is T1 (CENTCOM/US DoD).
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM: the blockade applies to ALL vessels of ALL nations entering/leaving Iranian ports -- directly contradicting 'the Americans do not intercept them either'. Al Mayeda (Qatari LNG carrier, exempted nationality) was struck Oct 30 despite Iranian clearance. No independent shipping data confirms exempted vessels actually transiting freely; the strait remains almost completely closed with ~2,000 ships stranded (AJ, Nov 7). PORTWATCH: newest local snapshot portwatch-2026-10-26.json is STALE (latest observation Oct 18: 4 transits, 2 tanker, 7-day avg 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day) -- cite only as the stale Oct 18 count, never as live. GAP: CrisisBrief's Nov 7 briefing cites a newer PortWatch observation (2 transits on Oct 25) that is NOT in our local snapshot; the pull has not refreshed since Oct 26 -- flag to the newsroom, do not present the Oct 25 figure as our counted number.
sections.why_matters: Iran has turned the closed strait into a toll road: four countries pass, two pay, one rides free -- and Washington says it will intercept them anyway. Hard numbers: 10.23 million barrels a day in October, 42% to China, 13% to India. The exemption is real; the safety is not -- Al Mayeda proved it.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (AJ explainer published 2026-11-06T06:06:24Z; ISNA interview Tue Nov 3; zero 'Moqaddam'/'exempt' mentions in any prior Nov 6/7 scan -- grep confirms) -- Iran exempts ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar from Strait of Hormuz restrictions; Tehran charges transit fees to Indian and Chinese ships, Qatari ships pass free; 'Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either'

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran has turned the closed strait into a toll road: four countries pass, two pay, one rides free -- and Washington says it will intercept them anyway. Hard numbers: 10.23 million barrels a day in October, 42% to China, 13% to India. The exemption is real; the safety is not -- Al Mayeda proved it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Tehran is now selling passage through the world's oil artery -- tolls for India and China, free for Qatar. Is this a lifeline that keeps oil moving, or a blockade-busting toll booth that CENTCOM says it will still stop? And who pays when an 'exempt' ship gets hit anyway, like Al Mayeda?
